newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen's troops tighten grip on Cambodian capital.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen's troops tighten grip on Cambodian capital.

text.p: The Cambodian capital was rocked by heavy fighting for a second day on Sunday as forces under Second Prime Minister Hun Sen tightened their grip on the city.

Shelling and small arms fire began before dawn and continued sporadically through the day, spreading into the heart of the city as Hun Sen's forces battled those of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Ranariddh's official residence, his FUNCINPEC party headquarters and the French Embassy next door were both heavily damaged, officials said. The fighting began on Saturday but by Sunday afternoon troops loyal to Hun Sen were moving through the city street by street as heavy fighting continued around pockets of Ranariddh's men.

Military officials loyal to Hun Sen said they were demanding the surrender of Ranariddh's troops protecting some of his facilities. But Ranariddh's top military commander, General Nhiek Bun Chhay, vowed earlier that there would be no surrender.
The casualty toll was impossible to determine but at least 12 people had been killed and more than 50 wounded since the violence began, hospital sources and local news reports said.
A 38-year old Japanese man died from his wounds after a rocket hit his house, a foreign ministry official in Tokyo said.
An official at one city hospital said medical supplies
would start running out if the fighting continued much longer.

The heaviest fighting raged around key facilities under the control of forces loyal to Ranariddh, including a well-defended compound, a base near the international airport, Ranariddh's party headquarters and his residence -- all of which were protected by his security men and troops.
A huge cloud of black smoke from a burning fuel station or factory hung over the city as several other buildings burned in the vicinity of the fighting.

It was not clear if the fighting would last long into the night as local authorities had declared a curfew from 8 pm to 6 am (1300-2300 GMT). The city fell relatively quiet on Saturday night after a similar curfew was imposed.
The road to the airport remained closed and all flights in and out of the city were cancelled.
The French Embassy was heavily damaged in the day's fighting.
"We've been hit by some heavy cannon. The ambassador's office and the office of the military attache were completely destroyed," an official at the embassy said.
France is the former colonial power in Cambodia but there was no suggestion that the building had been deliberately targeted.

Fifteeen embassy staff, French and Cambodian, were in the embassy when it was hit but none was injured, he said. The embassy official said Hun Sen's troops appeared to have taken control of the FUNCINPEC headquarters next door.
U.S. Ambassador Kenneth Quinn told reporters many soldiers loyal to Hun Sen were moving around his embassy. He said he had forcefully conveyed his concerns to Hun Sen's office.

"People don't deserve to be caught up in fighting like this," Quinn said. As booms echoed over the riverside city, thousands of people laden with bundles of clothes, food and televisions streamed out of neighbourhoods where the fighting was heaviest. Many said they were leaving the city.
Markets opened briefly just after dawn and shoppers said prices had doubled overnight.
Hotels were packed with local residents, political officials and diplomats seeking refuge. Some hotel managers said they were running out of food.

Ranariddh said in a statement from Paris that Hun Sen was attempting a coup. Radio and television stations controlled by Hun Sen denied a coup was under way and urged people to remain calm as government troops were only fighting Khmer Rouge guerrillas.

Radio and television stations controlled by Ranariddh's party were off the air and most international and local telephone lines were down. A member of Ranariddh's cabinet who was holed up at the prince's walled, city-centre compound told Reuters by telephone that the compound was under intermittent fire and one explosion had severely damaged one of the buildings in the compound.
